note: ADR-0006 template-owned path boundary. Ownership is resolved by longest matching prefix; a prefix ending in '/' matches a directory subtree, otherwise it matches an exact file. On a tie, user-owned wins (fail-closed: an upgrade never touches a path it isn't sure the template owns). Conservatively excludes apps/ (portal carries user/plugin pages) and infra/environments/ (per-instance config and secrets) for now; that boundary can widen later. services/api/migrations/versions/ is user-owned even though services/api/ is template-owned: Alembic migration files are an append-only, per-instance chain (each instance accumulates its own, chained by down_revision), so syncing them from the template breaks the instance's revision graph. The migration framework itself (migrations/env.py, script.py.mako) stays template-owned. docs/ADR/ is user-owned: the template's ADRs are seeded once at `biffo init` as a starting point, but an instance's ADRs are its own decision record and legitimately diverge from the Biffo standard over time — force-syncing them on every core upgrade collides an instance's own ADR numbers with the template's and rewrites its history. Excluded from the sync flow for that reason; new template ADRs are announced in release notes rather than pushed into instances. core.version is deliberately absent from both lists (so it is user-owned by fail-closed default and never synced): it is the version the *template emits*, its own source of truth, while the version an instance *received* is recorded in the userOwned biffo.core.json — which already wins on every read (cli/src/lib/core-version.ts), leaving the inherited core.version as a mere fallback. Syncing core.version into an instance therefore cannot improve any lookup; it can only overwrite whatever the instance keeps there (one instance repurposed it as its own app release lineage, which an upgrade would regress).
